title: A Walkable ASCII Cyberpunk City in One HTML File
description:
Update: With the recent release of Prototype 2, I've made Prototype 1 free to access: https://ko-fi.com/grownowgames/shop

I wanted to build a city that feels alive, but is made entirely from ASCII characters.

This is a small custom engine built with JavaScript and Canvas — no Unity, Unreal, 3D models, textures, or shaders. The world is a grid-based city with roads, buildings, trees, cars, and pedestrians. 

Every frame, the engine raycasts from the camera to work out perspective, depth, collisions, and what should be visible, then draws it all using letters, numbers, and symbols.

In other words: it’s a tiny 3D city made from blocks, viewed through a screen of ASCII characters.

Still a work in progress, but I’m going to keep pushing the atmosphere, detail, and interaction further.

#ASCII #ASCIICity #Cyberpunk #IndieDev #GameDev #JavaScript #HTML5Canvas #Raycasting #CreativeCoding #ProceduralGeneration #CodingProject

title: I Built a Custom GPU-Driven Rendering Pipeline (10x Faster)
description:
Support PlanetSmith & Alpha Access: https://planetsmith.world/store?utm_source=Devlog25
Wishlist on Steam: https://store.steampowered.com/app/2539340/PlanetSmith/ 
Join our Discord: https://discord.gg/eSS2pYU7Nw

In my last devlog I replaced physics meshes with a custom voxel system. That got me thinking, could I do the same for rendering? Turns out yes, and the results are wild.

In this devlog I build a custom GPU-driven rendering pipeline using indirect rendering, upload vertex data straight to the GPU with no mesh objects at all, add octree-based frustum culling that runs entirely on the graphics card, and compress our vertex format down to a fraction of its original size. End result: a 10x performance boost, planets rendered at full detail, and over a billion vertices on screen at once.

title: Slow walk through a convolutional neural network
description:
Inference of a handwritten digit of the MNIST dataset represented as a 28x28 pixel raster image is shown in a hopefully clear way. The convolutional neural network, CNN, is scarcely trained for the sole purpose of the final probabilities to be slightly more spread out. Further, the architecture is just an example, although it seems working pretty well for sufficiently trained weights/filters. 

This is a re-upload. This since the original had some annoying re-encoding glitches I couldn't stand.

Music by  @gpcbass , called SevenEight made yesterday.

Languages/tools: Python, JavaScript, GPT 6 Astra, FFmpeg
